question: Should memory-lancedb autoCapture reject OpenClaw-authored external-content wrappers by default, or should this be exposed as a new `captureFilter` configuration option?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent security boundary determines whether trust is framework-owned by default or delegated to operator configuration, and cleanup automation should not choose that policy.

options.title: Reject wrappers by default
options.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/tool content.

options.title: Add captureFilter config
options.body: Introduce a documented operator-controlled `excludeWrapped` option, with schema, manifest, docs, and upgrade-safe default tests.

options.title: Fold into provenance design
options.body: Defer this narrow filter until the broader memory trust/provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject wrappers by default
recommendation.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web/browser/tool content.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal on external-content wrapper hardening and the security seam this decision crosses.
